summary: Mentor can now tell you in simple words what each update brings, and its version reads like a date.
Mentor Settings has an Updates tab: every update this Mentor had, and Ask Mentor to go over one with you.
Mentor now warns you and asks first before it restarts to install an update.
In Mentor Settings, Updates, the list of updates is sorted by year and month.
Mentor Settings now uses the whole width of the window, like the Recipes app.
When something does not work as expected, you can tell Mentor's maker: right-click the desktop, Report a problem.
A shorter desktop menu, and the bell's suggestions now have their own tab in Mentor Settings.
In the Recipes app, switching a recipe off only switches it off, and a widget's switch works at once.
Every card in the chat can now be talked about, update cards no longer pop up, and switching a recipe off asks first.
Mentor Settings is back in the desktop menu, next to Settings, and the menu now stays exactly as it is.
Mentor Settings has its own icon: the Mentor owl.
Mentor's self-check now also makes sure Mentor keeps getting its updates.
The bell now has More buttons for more GitHub projects, apps and news, from more sources. History shows the question each answer was for.
The gear now turns while Mentor works on your request, and the bell opens narrow when it has no cards.
Make the chat's text larger or smaller with Ctrl and the mouse wheel (or Ctrl + + − 0); the cards widen with it, and Mentor remembers the size.
Mouse-look now works in 3D games: Mentor switches to a game mouse by itself while a game is in front. The Recipes app can delete a recipe.
Mentor now tells you in the chat when a program crashes, and full system upgrades are safer: fresh signing keys first, a free-space check, and a check of the start-up files.
No more false warning after your computer sleeps: Mentor's own checks no longer look broken when Windows pauses Mentor.
Settings no longer freezes after Mouse & Touchpad, about 37 languages can be chosen in Settings, and the assistant's text box always stays in view.
The setup screens show the simpler Mentor owl.
Copy text from anything on the screen with Shift+Super+T, reminders in the chat, websites as apps of their own, and games set up when you ask.
Maximizing Mentor's window or making it full screen no longer shows everything small for a moment.
Mentor follows your Windows time zone, and you can approve its password questions with Windows Hello (with the new Mentor program on Windows).
Your laptop's volume keys, Windows' volume and Mentor's volume are now one and the same (with the newest Mentor program on Windows).
Your laptop's volume keys, Windows' volume and Mentor's volume are one and the same, one step per key press (with the newest Mentor program on Windows).
Small fixes: zooming the chat works right after a start, cards no longer hide under the Super+Z box, and copying text from the screen is more reliable.
More small fixes: problem reports leave out passwords written in words, recipe checks list every command, and fewer false alarms in the logs.
Changing your password is easier: Mentor Settings opens a simple window for it instead of a text window.
Clearer recipe checks: the list of what a recipe would run is complete and holds only commands.
Chromium and apps open smoothly: no empty terms window the first time, and the assistant can open them with every engine.
The assistant recovers from its own small mistakes: when it asks a tool for something in the wrong form, it is told and tries again, instead of stopping in the middle of your request.
